title: Josh Heupel Finishes Second for the 2000 Heisman Trophy
question: Who was Oklahoma's quarterback runner-up for the 2000 Heisman Trophy?
answer: Josh Heupel finished second to Florida State's Chris Weinke in the 2000 Heisman voting, 1,628 points to 1,552. He was also named the AP College Football Player of the Year before leading Oklahoma to a 13-0 national championship season.
summary: Josh Heupel was the 2000 Heisman runner-up, just 76 points behind Chris Weinke, and led Oklahoma to a 13-0 national title. Here is how it unfolded.
body: The 2000 Heisman Trophy race came down to two quarterbacks. Florida State's Chris Weinke won it with 1,628 points, and Oklahoma's Josh Heupel was second with 1,552, a margin of just 76 points. Heupel received 286 first-place votes, so the finish was far closer than a typical runner-up result.

Heupel was the engine of a Sooner offense that helped turn Bob Stoops' second season into a title run. Contemporary coverage reported him as the Associated Press College Football Player of the Year, a national honor that reflected how central he was to Oklahoma's unbeaten year.

Not every honor went his way. Weinke took the Davey O'Brien Award that year, and Purdue's Drew Brees won the Maxwell Award according to ESPN's awards coverage, so fans who tally Heupel's trophies should check which lists they trust.

The Heisman rarity added a final twist. Winner and runner-up met on the field in the Orange Bowl for the national championship, and Oklahoma won 13-2 on January 3, 2001. That result finished a 13-0 season and gave the Sooners their seventh national title, with Heupel remembered as the quarterback who led the way.
